anomalies: A == B == 116 exactly: this family has ZERO loose-only Obsolete variants - there is no 'Obsolete for documents created in ...' or 'Obsolete and not superseded. ...' form anywhere in its headers, so A minus B is 0 and the two criteria cannot disagree here.

IFeatureFillet2 writes the pointer marker with a CAPITAL I ('In-process, unmanaged C++', 5 hits) while the other four pages use lowercase ('in-process, unmanaged C++'); a strictly case-sensitive literal search scores IFeatureFillet2 as 0 and would report D=3. I counted it (D=4) with case-insensitive matching - the criterion was read as referring to the marker, not to its capitalization.

FeatureName is the only page with no **Signature** line (G=1): its frontmatter says kind: property but the whole body is just the H1 heading - no Returns, no See Also, no Examples. It is therefore the 23rd property page by frontmatter while F=22 is derived from actual no-parenthesis signatures; the two disagree by exactly this stub.

8 pages mention 'obsolete' only AFTER the **Signature** line, inside Remarks prose, and are counted by neither A nor B because both criteria are header-scoped: FeatureExtrusion3, FeatureFillet3, FeatureRevolve2, InsertCutSwept5, InsertProtrusionSwept4, InsertSweepSurface3, InsertWrapFeature2, PreSplitBody2. InsertProtrusionSwept4 / InsertCutSwept5 / InsertSweepSurface3 are NOT marked Obsolete in their own header ('SOLIDWORKS 2018 introduces a new sweep architecture, making this method obsolete'), so a reader who greps the whole file instead of the header would overcount.

Of the 28 zero-arg members, 3 (HideBodies, ShowBodies, UpdateFeatureTree) are void and have NO '## Returns' section at all, so ranking candidates by Returns text length necessarily pushes them to zero - they are real zero-arg methods with no Returns text, not missing pages.

The family contains 11 I-prefixed (in-process naming convention) members but only 5 carry the literal pointer marker: IInsertMacroFeature, IInsertMacroFeature2, IInsertMacroFeature3, IInsertReferencePoint, IInsertSheetMetalEdgeFlange2 and IInsertTableDrivenPattern have no marker anywhere in the page. The I prefix alone must therefore NOT be used as a pointer proxy - it would give 11 instead of 5.

E was derived as raw zero-parenthesis signatures (38) minus obsolete (10) minus pointer (0) = 28; the 10 excluded obsolete zero-arg members are AddSMNormalCut, CreateFormTool, FeatureAdvancedTableDrivenPattern, FinishSMNormalCut, GetFeatureTreeRootItem, InsertDeleteBody, InsertDerivedPattern, InsertDerivedPattern2, InsertFeatureTreeFolder and PreSplitBody.
No page has a signature containing parentheses AND {get, so splitting E from F purely on the presence of '(' is unambiguous; no signature failed to parse out of its backticks (0 unparsed of 285).

Arithmetic cross-check that ties the whole corpus together: 22 properties (no parens) + 38 zero-paren methods + 225 methods with parameters = 285 pages with a signature, plus the 1 stub page = 286 = members_total.

Checked for undercount of C: zero pages have a '## Returns' section mentioning 'Pointer to an array' while lacking the in-process marker, so no pointer member is being missed by keying on that literal string.
